tools.name: animation_editor
tools.description:
Creates and modifies animations (state machines, linear animations, keyframes) on the active artboard. Falls back to the first artboard when none is activated; use query_core_object_tool.listArtboards to disambiguate.
REUSE THE DEFAULTS - a new artboard already has one timeline named "Timeline" and one default state machine (isDefault=true) whose Entry is already connected to that timeline. To animate the artboard:
  1. renameAnimations to rename the "Timeline" to something meaningful (e.g. "Bounce").
  2. modifyKeyFrames to add keyframes to that same timeline.
This applies when creating SEVERAL animations too: if the default timeline is still pristine (default name, no keyframes), rename it to the FIRST of them, then use createLinearAnimations only for the remaining ones - never leave a stale "Timeline"/"Timeline 1" behind next to your named animations. If the user has already renamed or keyed it, leave it alone and create all animations fresh.
Do NOT call createLinearAnimations or createStateMachine for this - a second timeline or state machine is almost always wrong. Only create new ones when the user explicitly asks for an additional animation or state machine.
Special state names: "{Entry State}", "{Any State}". Between two keyframes the smaller-frame keyframe's interpolator (hold/linear/cubic/elastic) drives the curve. Commands: createStateMachine, createStateMachineLayers, createTransitions, createConditions, createLinearAnimations: create the named entity; createStates: Add new animation states to an EXISTING layer (use this when the layer already exists; createStateMachineLayers spawns a new layer instead); Listeners are created with the create_listeners tool (not here); this tool reads them via queryStateMachine and drives their state changes via createConditions; updateConditions: change an existing condition's operation, compared value, or viewmodel property (ids from queryStateMachine); deleteConditions: remove conditions by id; listStateMachines: id/name/layers only — for inspection use queryStateMachine; listLinearAnimations: all linear animations; queryStateMachine: PRIMARY read. Fully expands a state machine — layers with states/transitions/conditions/events/listenerActions, plus top-level inputs and listeners. View-model, event, and input refs are pre-resolved with names. Defaults to the only state machine; pass stateMachineId to disambiguate; queryStateMachineLayer: Re-read one layer (same per-layer payload); updateStates: Update existing states; renameAnimations: Rename animations; modifyKeyFrames: Add/delete/change keyframes. Double values use the units the editor UI shows: opacity/trim/strength as 0-100 percentages, rotation in degrees; queryKeyFrames: Read keyframes; simulateStateMachine: VERIFY a machine actually runs. Plays it headlessly and returns the same console trace the editor panel shows (frames, states entered, transitions taken, events fired), plus the resting state per layer. Drive it with inputs [{frame, property, value}] on viewmodel properties. Use after wiring conditions/listeners to confirm the machine leaves Entry and reaches the state you expect; an empty trace means nothing fired. Reverts the values it writes, so the document is unchanged, but it does run listener actions (including scripts) as real playback would; it does not render pixels. transitionsObserved counts the transitions taken (the default layer takes one unconditionally, so compare a driven run against an undriven one). Refuses to run while a timeline or state machine is open for editing. reverseKeyFrames: Reverse keyframes (scope: selection, else visible graph curves, else all). Data is passed under data.<command> or directly in data.

linearAnimationName.description: Name of an existing linear animation on the artboard. If unresolvable, the state is still created but a warning is emitted.

transitions.description: Inline transitions; from/to match state names declared in this same payload.

operation.description: Alias of comparationOperation (the key queryStateMachine emits).

value.description: Constant to compare against (or a viewModelPropertyId when valueType is viewModelType). Booleans accept true/false. Colors use #aarrggbb.

leftComparator.description: Retarget the condition to another viewmodel property. May replace the condition; the result echoes the live id.

cubicParams.description: Parameters for cubic interpolation. x1, x2 in [0, 1], y1, y2 in [-1, 1]

amplitude.description: A percentage of change, defaults to 1.0

period.description: Percentage of time difference, defaults to 1.0

tools.name: create_listeners
tools.description: Creates state machine listeners for interactivity (hover, click, drag). Every listener requires a target component (targetId or targetName) - untargeted listeners are not exported at runtime. For artboard-wide pointer input, add a background shape covering the artboard and target that (pointer inputs are not offered on artboard targets); the artboard itself is targetable by its own name for event/viewModel inputs. Listener inputs react to pointer, event, or view-model signals and run actions: viewModelChange (set a bound property, optionally to a constant value; on a trigger property this fires the trigger - the preferred way to signal runtime code), alignTarget, fireEvent (Rive Events are legacy for runtime signaling - audio/open-URL only), scripted. For hover/press driven state changes: add a boolean viewmodel property, create enter+exit (or down+up) listeners that viewModelChange it true/false, then animation_editor createConditions on the transitions against it. Use animation_editor queryStateMachine to inspect existing listeners. Defaults to the only state machine when stateMachineId is omitted.

stateMachineId.description: Optional. Defaults to the only state machine on the active artboard. References resolve against the machine's own artboard.

name.description: Optional display name. Defaults to the target component name.

targetName.description: Component to listen on, by name (shape, layout, text run, or the artboard itself). One of targetId / targetName is required.

listenerTypes.description: When omitted, defaults to a single "enter" input (the editor default).

value.description: Optional constant for viewModelChange (number/bool/string/"#aarrggbb" color). Omit on trigger properties - the action fires the trigger. Mutually exclusive with sourceViewModelPropertyId.

sourceViewModelPropertyId.description: Write another viewmodel property's live value instead of a constant (the inspector's Property value mode). Use to record which list item was hit: source a list index property into a number property.

tools.name: assets_tool
tools.description: Read and instantiate assets (images, audio, fonts, scripts, libraries, components, blobs, svg, lottie). listAssets: Folder-grouped tree; queryAsset: One asset by id; addImageInstance: Spawn an Image shape from an ImageAsset; addImagesAsSolo: Spawn a Solo of Images (no input/VM wiring); addSvgInstance: Import an SVGAsset as an editable shape hierarchy under a Node.

typeFilter.description: Optional. One of: image, audio, font, script, library, component, svg, lottie, file, folder, group, componentGroup. Folders are still walked.

tools.name: upload_asset
tools.description: Adds ONE image (png/jpeg/webp), SVG, font (ttf/otf), or audio (mp3/wav/flac) asset to the currently open file. Returns the new asset's id and metadata. Does NOT place anything on the stage: instantiating the asset onto an artboard is a separate operation (assets_tool's addImageInstance or addSvgInstance).

file.description: The asset to add. Preferred: an RFC 2397 data URI of the form data:<mediatype>;name=<url-encoded-filename>;base64,<data>. Also accepted (localhost only): an absolute local filesystem path or a file:// URI to the asset on disk. The asset type is detected automatically: images, fonts and SVG from the file content, and audio from the filename extension (an audio data URI's name=, or a local path, must end in .mp3, .wav, or .flac). An SVG that opens with an XML declaration instead of <svg needs mediatype image/svg+xml or a .svg filename. If a local path fails with a permission error (the editor may be sandboxed, e.g. on macOS), retry with a data URI — it requires no file access by the editor. Do not generate the base64 yourself; the permission-error result includes a step-by-step curl recipe for scripting the upload.

name.description: Optional display name for the new asset (extension omitted; a recognized asset extension is stripped if included). Defaults to the uploaded filename.

tools.name: upload_rev
tools.description: Uploads a Rive document (.rev, the native coop-serialized format) to one of two destinations, chosen by the required "target" parameter: "open_file" imports it into the currently open file, which must be empty; "current_project" instead uploads it as a brand-new file in the open file's project, leaving the open file untouched, and returns the new file's id.

file.description: The .rev document to upload. Preferred: an RFC 2397 data URI of the form data:<mediatype>;name=<url-encoded-filename>;base64,<data> (mediatype can be application/octet-stream; .rev has no registered MIME type). Also accepted (localhost only): an absolute local filesystem path or a file:// URI to the .rev on disk. The content is validated as a coop revision regardless of filename. If a local path fails with a permission error (the editor may be sandboxed, e.g. on macOS), retry with a data URI — it requires no file access by the editor. Do not generate the base64 yourself; the permission-error result includes a step-by-step curl recipe for scripting the upload.

target.description: Where to put the uploaded document. "open_file" imports it into the currently open file, which must be empty (no existing content) — the import fails otherwise. "current_project" instead uploads it as a brand-new file in the open file's project, leaving the open file untouched, and returns the new file's id.

tools.name: export_file
tools.description: Exports the currently open document to disk. `format` chooses between the runtime format (.riv, for embedding in an app) and the native backup format (.rev, a full editable revision). The export snapshots the in-memory document AS IT CURRENTLY IS, including any unsaved changes. The file is written into `destination` and the result reports the full path written; an existing file at that path is never overwritten. Either format may need network access to complete: a .rev export needs it when embed_assets is on, and a .riv export needs it whenever the document references hosted assets, since their CDN ids are resolved during export. Both formats are typically plan-gated together — if one is refused as an upgrade feature, do not try the other as a workaround.

format.description: The export format. 'riv' is the editor's "Export > For Runtime" action: a .riv file meant to be loaded by a Rive runtime in an app. 'rev' is the editor's "Export > For Backup" action: a .rev native coop file that can be reopened and edited in this editor, meant as a personal backup. There is no default; the caller must choose.

destination.description: Absolute path of an EXISTING directory on this machine to write the export into. Pass your own working directory unless the user names somewhere else. The filename is derived from the open document's name, and the result reports the full path written. An existing file at that path is never overwritten.

embed_assets.description: Only meaningful for format "rev". When true (the default, matching the editor's backup export), every asset the document references is downloaded and embedded in the .rev file, which needs network access. Pass false to export a document-only revision with no asset downloads.

inline_base64.description: For scripted retries only; default false. This tool ALWAYS tries to write the export to disk first, and only returns the bytes as inline base64 when that write is refused for permissions. This flag exists to enable that fallback for the shell recipe returned in the permission-denied error — do not set it speculatively.

tools.name: tag_editor
tools.description: Read and manage tags: colored labels that organize components, animations, assets, and viewmodel properties across the editor panels. Editor organization only - tags are NOT exported to the .riv and have no runtime behavior. queryTags: All tags with color, hidden/locked, tagged count; createTags: New tags (name, optional #rrggbb/#aarrggbb color, hidden, locked); updateTags: Rename/recolor/set hidden or locked; deleteTags: Delete tags (untags every object); assignTags/unassignTags: Apply or remove tags on objects (shapes, groups, animations, assets, viewmodel properties...). Write commands require a plan with tags and error if the workspace lacks it.

includeTaggedObjects.description: Include per-tag id/name/type of every tagged object. Default false (counts only).

tagName.description: Alternative to tagId; errors if the name is ambiguous.

tools.name: component_editor
tools.description: Adds Components to other Artboards. When a Component Artboard has a ViewModel bound, we should try to hook it up to the parent Artboard's ViewModel as a property. Supports commands like,addComponents: Adds a Component as a child of the given parent on the specified artboard; addComponentList: Adds a Component list container as a child of the given parent on the specified artboard where the parent determines the list's layout. A Component List automatically generates component instances at runtime based on the specified ViewModelPropertyList id so DO NOT manually add Components as children of the list. Use instead of 'addComponents' whenever a list of items is required;

widthScaleType.description: The width scale type of the component when in layout mode. fixed = fixed size, fill = fills its parent layout, hug = lets its children determine its size

heightScaleType.description: The height scale type of the component when in layout mode. fixed = fixed size, fill = fills its parent layout, hug = lets its children determine its size

tools.name: open_file_editor
tools.description:
Manage artboards in the file.

Commands:
- getCurrentFile: identify this file: name, location, and editor url. Rive files live in the cloud, so there is no path on disk.
- listArtboards: list all artboards (name, size, position).
- getSelectedArtboard: get the active/selected artboard.
- focusArtboard: make an artboard active by id or name.
- renameArtboard: rename artboards by id or name.
- arrangeArtboard: move artboards to a new x/y position.
- resizeArtboard: change artboard width and/or height.
- createArtboard: create one or more artboards. Do NOT set x/y unless the user asks for an exact position. Rive automatically places each new artboard in free space (so it never covers an existing artboard) and moves the view to show it - you do not need to position, focus, or scroll to it yourself.
- closeRevisionHistory: close the Revision History panel. While it is open the file is view only and all editing commands fail; close it only when the user wants to resume editing.
- undo: revert the last change you made.

artboardName.description: The name of the artboard to focus

fitToViewport.description: Whether to fit the artboard into the viewport

artboardName.description: The current name of the artboard to rename

newName.description: The new name for the artboard

y.description: Exact Y position. Leave unset in almost all cases: Rive auto-places the artboard in free space. Only set it when the user gives a specific location.

isComponent.description: Whether this artboard can be used as a Component in other Artboards

tools.name: session_info
tools.description: List the files open in the editor and which tab is active. Read-only. Rive files live in the cloud, so there is no path on disk; use the returned url to refer to a file.

tools.name: layout_editor
tools.description:
Creates UI layouts with flexbox-style positioning, padding, gaps, and alignment. Use this for structured user interfaces.

USE THIS TOOL for:
- UI components (buttons, cards, modals, navigation bars)
- Screen layouts and page structures
- Lists, grids, and content containers
- Text with layout positioning (do NOT use emoji characters)
- Anything requiring flexbox arrangement (rows, columns, wrapping)
- 2-D grids (set layoutStyle.layoutType="grid" and define templateColumns/templateRows) -- may be unavailable on this host; the call fails with guidance if so
- Stacks / overlapping z-ordered content (set layoutStyle.layoutType="stack"; align with `alignment`) -- may be unavailable on this host; the call fails with guidance if so
- Rotated/scaled layouts with a pivot (set the `transform` object; also settable on existing layouts via setPropertyValues)

Layouts can be children of other layouts, the artboard, or a transparent container (a group or Solo).
Text children participate in the layout directly (sized by their layoutStyle width/height scale type) — no wrapper layout. To give text its own background/padding, put it inside its own child layout.
Commands: createLayout (new layout tree), appendLayout (add children), setLayoutVisibility (show/hide layouts - the eye icon on a layout in the inspector, i.e. display: none; hidden layouts render nothing and take no space)

artboardId.description: The artboard to create the layout on. When omitted, falls back to the host's current artboard if it has one; a host with no ambient artboard fails the call instead of guessing.

layoutType.description: Layout mode (default flex). flex = flexbox row/column via flexDirection; grid = 2-D grid, define templateColumns/templateRows below; stack = children overlap (z-ordered), positioned by `alignment`.

type.description: Track sizing function. fr = fraction of free space, points = fixed px, percent = % of container, auto = content-sized.

tools.name: group_editor
tools.description: Create a group (a Node). Pass objectIds to wrap those objects in a group, preserving their on-screen positions and draw order like the editor Group command. Omit objectIds for an empty group to parent things under later. Use this instead of duplicating an existing group.

objectIds.description: Objects to wrap. An object listed together with one of its ancestors is wrapped inside that ancestor, not separately. Omit for an empty group.

name.description: Name for the group. Defaults to "Group".

parentId.description: Parent for an EMPTY group; defaults to the active artboard. Rejected together with objectIds, since a wrapping group takes the place of what it wraps.

x.description: X for an empty group, in editor units. Defaults to 0. Ignored when wrapping.

y.description: Y for an empty group, in editor units. Defaults to 0. Ignored when wrapping.

tools.name: property_group_editor
tools.description: Creates Custom Property Groups and the typed Custom Properties they contain on a parent (artboard or any container component). The resulting properties can be data-bound (use viewmodel_editor databind with the property's id and returned bindKey) and keyframed on a timeline (use animation_editor with the same id and returned keyframeKey, which is type-specific such as firePropertyKey for triggers). NOT for interactivity: listeners and transition conditions read ViewModel properties (viewmodel_editor), not custom properties. Property types: number, boolean, color, string, enum, trigger. Commands: addPropertyGroups: Creates one or more property groups, each with an optional initial set of properties; addPropertiesToGroup: Adds properties to an existing group.

parentId.description: ID of the parent ContainerComponent (artboard or any container component) to attach the group to.

name.description: Optional name for the property group.

properties.description: List of typed custom properties to create in the group.

value.description: Optional initial value. number=double, boolean=bool, color=#aarrggbb string, string=string, enum=enum value name (matched against the enum referenced by enumId), trigger ignored.

enumId.description: Required for enum properties: id of the DataEnum that defines this property's allowed values.

groupId.description: ID of the existing CustomPropertyGroup to add properties to.

properties.description: List of typed custom properties to create in the group.

value.description: Optional initial value. number=double, boolean=bool, color=#aarrggbb string, string=string, enum=enum value name (matched against the enum referenced by enumId), trigger ignored.

enumId.description: Required for enum properties: id of the DataEnum that defines this property's allowed values.

tools.name: viewmodel_editor
tools.description: Creates and manages view models and their instances. Supports commands like,listViewModels: Lists all view models; createViewModels: Creates view models with properties; createViewModelInstances: Creates instances of a view model; addProperties: Adds properties to existing view models. A viewModel-typed property references another view model by viewModelId (preferred) or viewModelName, which may name one created in the same call; databind: Makes the value of an object's property come from a viewmodel instance. When binding strings to text, you must bind to the Text Run, not the Text object itself. Re-running databind on an already-bound object property retargets the existing bind. Properties on nested viewmodels need path when several routes reach them; isRelative makes the bind resolve by names from the bound instance (the relative toggle); modifyDataBind: Modifies an existing data bind's direction (toTarget, toSource, twoWay), once flag, source-to-target ordering, attached converter, source path, or relative flag; bindViewModelToArtboard: Binds a viewmodel instance to an artboard; bindViewModelToComponent: Sets a component placement's own data context (the Model/Path rows in the inspector). Use this - not raw property writes - to point each placement of the same component at its own viewmodel property, clear it back to inherit, or assign a specific instance. Accepts multiple placements at once. Not available for stateful components (their instance is auto-managed); listViewModelInstances: Lists all view model instances from a view model; listDataBinds: Lists existing data binds with their source paths and flags; createConverters: Creates data converters to transform a bound value (for example convertToString so a number property can drive a text run). Pass the returned id as a binding's converterId in databind, then tune settings with query_core_object_tool setPropertyValues. Use a group to chain several transforms into one converter (its children are created or reused in the same call) and a formula for arithmetic. Check listConverters first and reuse a match: converters cannot be deleted here, so one created by mistake stays in the data panel for the user to remove; listConverters: Lists existing converters with their type and id, so one can be reused instead of creating a duplicate; listDataEnums: Lists enums (the Enums section of the data panel) with their values; createDataEnums: Creates enums and their values. Create the enum before an enum property that uses it; addDataEnumValues: Appends values to an existing enum; removeDataEnumValues: Removes values from an enum; deleteDataEnums: Deletes whole enums and their values. Needs force: true to delete one that still backs properties, and sweeps any library assets the removal leaves unused. An enum property is a viewModelProperties entry with propertyType enum plus enumName or enumId;

oneOf.description: Exposes an item's position in the list that holds it. One per viewmodel; always named "index" (the name field is ignored). Read-only: bind or condition on it, and write it into a number property via a create_listeners viewModelChange sourceViewModelPropertyId.

enumName.description: Name of the DataEnum backing this property. Create it first with createDataEnums.

enumId.description: Id of the DataEnum, as an alternative to enumName.

viewModelId.description: Id of the referenced view model. Preferred over viewModelName: names are not unique, and listViewModels emits both so its output feeds straight back in.

viewModelName.description: Name of the referenced view model. Resolves against view models created in this same call first, then existing ones. Ignored when viewModelId is given.

value.description: For enum properties, the value key as listed by listDataEnums.

childItems.description: Each item resolves an instance, most specific key first: viewModelInstanceId, else viewModelId/viewModelName plus optional viewModelInstanceName (default instance when omitted). An id that does not resolve is an error, never a fallback to the name.

oneOf.description: Exposes an item's position in the list that holds it. One per viewmodel; always named "index" (the name field is ignored). Read-only: bind or condition on it, and write it into a number property via a create_listeners viewModelChange sourceViewModelPropertyId.

enumName.description: Name of the DataEnum backing this property. Create it first with createDataEnums.

enumId.description: Id of the DataEnum, as an alternative to enumName.

viewModelId.description: Id of the referenced view model. Preferred over viewModelName: names are not unique, and listViewModels emits both so its output feeds straight back in.

viewModelName.description: Name of the referenced view model. Resolves against view models created in this same call first, then existing ones. Ignored when viewModelId is given.

viewModelId.description: The ID of the view model to bind to

objectId.description: The ID of the object to bind

propertyKey.description: The property key of the object property to bind

viewModelPropertyId.description: The ID of the view model property to bind to

path.description: Optional: the source path when the property lives on a nested/referenced viewmodel. Segment names joined with " -> " (the root viewmodel, then the viewmodel-property name of each hop), exactly as errors and listDataBinds list them. Required only when several paths reach the property.

A group with no children rejects every input. A child may itself be a group with its own children, nested to any depth — the levels spelled out below are a schema limitation, not a limit on what you can send.

tools.name: path_editor
tools.description:
Creates shapes in Rive. DEFAULT to createParametricShapes for any geometric primitive (rectangle, ellipse, triangle, polygon, star): e.g. "a box" or "a rounded rectangle" is a parametric rectangle with cornerRadius, NEVER hand-built from path commands. These are the same objects the editor shape tools make, with real editable properties (width, height, cornerRadius, points, innerRadius). Use createShapes with raw path commands ONLY for freeform/custom vectors that no primitive can express. IMPORTANT for createShapes: a shape is invisible without paths AND commands. Every shape MUST have at least one path with at least one moveTo and one lineTo/cubicTo. Every filled path MUST end with a close command. VALID paintType values (exact strings): "fill" or "stroke". VALID commandType values (exact strings): "moveTo" (requires x,y — sets the start point), "lineTo" (requires x,y — draws a straight segment), "cubicTo" (requires control1X,control1Y,control2X,control2Y,endX,endY — bezier curve), "close" (no args — closes the path back to moveTo point, required for fills). COORDINATE SYSTEM: A shape's x/y are in its PARENT's local space. Path commands are in the shape's OWN local space, drawn around (0,0). A layout's origin is its TOP-LEFT corner. A shape's x/y positions its center relative to that. To align a shape inside a layout, wrap it in a child layout the same size as the shape, set the PARENT layout's alignment, and place the shape at x=W/2, y=H/2 inside the child layout. Supports commands: createParametricShapes: Creates parametric primitives (rectangle/ellipse/triangle/polygon/star) with their editor properties; createShapes: Creates freeform shapes from raw path commands; addVertices: Adds vertices to an existing PointsPath by ID; addPaths: Adds new paths to an existing Shape by ID; addPaints: Adds new fills or strokes to an existing paint container by ID (a Shape, a LayoutComponent or Artboard for a background, or a text run's TextStylePaint); setPaints: Recolors EXISTING fills/strokes by ID, including switching a solid color to a linear/radial gradient or back; addGradientStops: Adds color stops to an existing gradient; removeGradientStops: Removes color stops from a gradient; addTrimPaths: Adds a trim path effect to existing fills/strokes by ID, trimming the rendered outline to a portion of its length. This is how a draw-on/write-on reveal is built: keyframe the trim start/end over time with animation_editor. start/end/offset are percentages (0-100), matching the inspector; mode is sequential (trims the paths end to end as one run) or synchronized (trims every path by the same amount). To retune an EXISTING trim, do not add a second one: queryObjects reports the effects on each paint with their ids, so write start/end/offset with query_core_object_tool setPropertyValues; To MOVE a gradient or retune one of its existing stops, do NOT use this tool: write the properties directly with query_core_object_tool setPropertyValues (the gradient's startX/startY/endX/endY and opacity, or a stop's position and colorValue). queryObjects reports gradientId and each stop id. combineShapes: Boolean-combines overlapping shapes (Shape Builder). merge unions the shapes into one; extractRegion pulls the region under a point into a new shape; eraseRegion deletes it. DESTRUCTIVE: flattens sources to plain paths and removes consumed shapes. Blocked when anything depends on the shapes and would not be removed with them (external dependents, cross-shape constraints, references into path geometry). When the operation would destroy animation keys (any keys on shapes it consumes; keys on path geometry of shapes it touches), the call errors listing them unless confirmKeyLoss: true is passed. Keys on a surviving shape's transform survive with it. Points are in artboard space; 

USE createParametricShapes for:
- Rectangles, squares (incl. rounded corners), circles, ellipses
- Triangles, polygons, stars
USE createShapes (raw paths) for:
- Freeform curves, arcs, custom silhouettes
- Simple lines, arrows, or connectors
- Shapes no parametric primitive can express

tools.name: mesh_rigging_tool
tools.description:
Rigs images AND vector shapes for skeletal (bone) animation: generate a deformable mesh, bind bones, and auto-compute vertex weights. This is the Edit Vertices/Mesh workflow (generate -> bind -> auto weight).

USE THIS TOOL for:
- Turning an image into a deformable mesh, traced to its outline (generateMesh)
- Binding one or more bones to a mesh OR a vector path (bindBones)
- Auto-computing how bones influence each vertex (autoWeight)
- Inspecting what bones are bound and their weights (querySkin)

IMPORTANT - binding and weighting work on BOTH image meshes and vector paths. A vector path is rigged directly through Edit Vertices (bindBones/autoWeight on the path); it does NOT need a generated mesh first. Only images need generateMesh before they can be bound.

generateMesh REQUIRES an image to act on. Pass imageId or imageName. If neither is given and nothing usable is selected, do NOT guess - tell the user to select the image they want to mesh, then try again.

Typical flow to rig an image: generateMesh -> bindBones -> autoWeight. For a vector path, skip generateMesh: bindBones -> autoWeight. Binding a target the first time auto-weights it, so a separate autoWeight call is only needed to re-run with different settings (blend/maxInfluences) or after changing the bones.

When several overlapping shapes are bound to the SAME bones (an arm split into upper-arm and forearm images), auto-weight them in ONE autoWeight call via targetIds/targetNames: they solve as one surface so the overlap deforms in unison. Weighting them in separate calls gives mismatched weights at the overlap and the artwork tears apart when the joint bends.

Does NOT create bones (use the component tool for that), animate them, or paint individual per-vertex weights.

Targets and bones may be referenced by id (preferred) or by name. maxInfluences is capped at 4 (the runtime limit of bones per vertex). blend is 0..1 where 0 is rigid (each vertex sticks to its nearest bone) and 1 is the widest blend at bone boundaries.

imageId.description: Id of the image to mesh.

imageName.description: Name of the image to mesh (used if imageId is omitted).

trace.description: Fit the mesh outline to the image silhouette instead of the default rectangle (default true). Set false only if the user explicitly wants a plain rectangular mesh.

detail.description: Trace detail 0..1: higher keeps more outline vertices (tighter fit), lower is coarser. Default 0.5. Only used when trace is true.

subdivisions.description: How many times to subdivide the generated mesh for denser interior geometry (0..4, default 0).

targetId.description: Id of the mesh or path (skinnable) to bind to.

targetName.description: Name of the mesh or path to bind to (used if targetId is omitted).

boneIds.description: Ids of the bones to bind.

boneNames.description: Names of the bones to bind (used for any bone not given by id).

targetId.description: Id of the bound mesh or path to auto-weight.

targetName.description: Name of the bound mesh or path to auto-weight.

targetIds.description: Ids of several bound meshes/paths to auto-weight together. Targets bound to the same bones solve as ONE surface so overlapping artwork deforms in unison; always pass all shapes of a multi-image rig in one call.

targetNames.description: Names of several bound meshes/paths to auto-weight together (used for any target not given by id).

blend.description: Blend width at bone boundaries 0..1 (0 rigid, 1 widest blend). Defaults to the editor's Blend default.

maxInfluences.description: Max bones influencing each vertex (1..4, default 4).

smooth.description: Smooth the weights across neighbors (default true).

targetId.description: Id of the mesh or path to inspect.

targetName.description: Name of the mesh or path to inspect.

includeVertexWeights.description: Also return the weights of every vertex (index, position, per-bone weight). Default false; the per-bone summary is usually enough.

tools.name: query_property_keys
tools.description: Get the available properties on objects by object IDs. Returns human-readable property names mapped to integer keys. Enum-backed properties also include an `enums` entry (propertyKey -> [name0, name1, ...]); the array index is the uint value to pass to set_property_values.

objectIds.description: Array of object IDs to query properties for

animates.description: Include only properties that can be animated

binds.description: Include only properties that can be used in databind

tools.name: query_objects
tools.description: Get id, type, name, and children for objects (depth-limited). If objectIds are not provided, defaults to currently selected objects.

objectIds.description: Array of object IDs to query for. If not provided, defaults to currently selected objects.

depth.description: Maximum depth to traverse children (0 = no children, 1 = direct children only, etc.). Defaults to 5 if not provided.

tools.name: query_property_values
tools.description: Get current values for object properties by object IDs and property keys. Numeric values are returned in the units the editor UI shows: percent-displayed properties (opacity, scale, trim path, constraint strength) as 0-100 style percentages, rotation in degrees.

propertyKeys.description: Object Id to array of property keys to get values for.

tools.name: find_objects
tools.description: Search for objects in the active artboard by name (case-insensitive substring) and/or type string. Use this to find an object ID when you only know its name or type.

name.description: Case-insensitive substring to match against object names. Omit to match any name.

type.description: Type string to filter by (e.g. "shape", "rectangle", "text", "group", "node", "ellipse", "artboard"). Omit to match any type.

parentId.description: Restrict the search to children of this object ID. Omit to search the entire active artboard.

tools.name: get_artboard_hierarchy
tools.description: Get the object tree of an artboard. Use depth=2 or depth=3 for a broad overview, then drill into specific branches. Avoid depth > 6 on complex artboards — the response can be very large.

artboardId.description: ID of the artboard to get the hierarchy for. Defaults to the active artboard if not provided.

depth.description: Maximum depth to traverse. Defaults to 5. Start shallow and increase only if you need to see deeper nesting. Large artboards at depth 20 can produce thousands of tokens.

tools.name: list_artboards
tools.description: List all artboards (id, name, isActive). For "what is the user working on": prefer selectionArtboardId (current selection) over isActive (sticky — persists across deselects).

tools.name: get_selection
tools.description: Returns the id, name, types, and parent id of every currently selected object in the editor.

inputSchema.description: Takes no input. Returns the currently selected objects in the editor.

tools.name: set_property_values
tools.description: Set values for object properties by object IDs and property keys. Numeric values use the units the editor UI shows: percent-displayed properties (opacity, scale, trim path, constraint strength) take 0-100 style percentages and rotation takes degrees; they are converted and clamped like inspector input. Invalid writes are rejected per-property in an errors list with machine-readable codes (invalid_enum_value, unknown_id, type_mismatch, read_only, ...).

propertyValues.description: Object Id to map of property keys to values: Map<Id, Map<int, int|string|color|bool>>

additionalProperties.description: Map of property keys to values. Values should match the property type (string, boolean, number, color string like #aarrggbb, or Id string).

tools.name: delete_objects
tools.description: Permanently delete objects from the file by their IDs.

objectIds.description: Array of object IDs to delete.

tools.name: rename_objects
tools.description: Rename objects by their IDs.

renames.description: List of id/name pairs to rename.

name.description: The new name for the object.

tools.name: select_objects
tools.description: Select objects in the editor by their IDs. Pass an empty array to clear the selection.

objectIds.description: Array of object IDs to select in the editor. Pass an empty array to clear the selection.

tools.name: duplicate_objects
tools.description: Duplicate objects by their IDs. Copies are placed as siblings of the originals.

objectIds.description: Array of object IDs to duplicate. Copies are placed as siblings of the originals.

tools.name: reorder_objects
tools.description: Change draw order (z-order): sendToFront, bringForward, sendBackward, or sendToBack.

tools.name: reparent_objects
tools.description: Move objects to a different parent in the hierarchy. Editor parenting rules apply (e.g. layouts parent to layouts, the artboard, or transparent containers like groups/Solos); invalid moves are rejected per-operation.

newParentId.description: The ID of the new parent. Any container component works (artboard, group, layout, solo, shape, bone, ...). Editor parenting rules apply, e.g. layouts parent to layouts, the artboard, or transparent containers (groups/Solos), and paths only live under shapes; invalid moves are rejected per-operation.

tools.name: capture_artboard
tools.description: Render an artboard to a PNG image so the model can examine what was actually produced, rather than inferring it from the object tree.

artboardId.description: Its id (as returned by `list_artboards`) or its exact name. When omitted, uses the artboard the editor is currently showing.

longEdge.description: Pixel length of the image's longer edge; the shorter edge follows the artboard's aspect ratio. Defaults to 512, clamped to 64–1536. The default size is sufficient for checking layout, composition, alignment, and color; request a larger size only when you need to read text or inspect fine detail, as cost scales with image area.

backgroundColor.description: Hex color: `#aarrggbb`, `#rrggbb`, or `0x…`. When omitted, the background is fully transparent, and transparent pixels mean "nothing was drawn there" — not black or white.

tools.name: manage_scripts
tools.description: Manages the LIFECYCLE of script and shader files: create, rename, move between folders, delete. Use this for any script/shader file-level operation. Does NOT edit script contents — to modify a script's source code, use text_editor. Commands: create: Creates one or more new Luau scripts or WGSL shaders, optionally seeded with content; rename: Renames one or more scripts/shaders by id or path (leaf name only — to relocate, use move); move: Moves one or more scripts/shaders to a target folder (missing folders are created); delete: Deletes one or more scripts/shaders.

name.description: Optional. Slashes group the script into folders, e.g. "utils/Math3D" places "Math3D" inside a "utils" folder (created if missing, reused on exact case-sensitive match). Trailing ".lua" / ".luau" / ".wgsl" / ".txt" is stripped automatically.

code_file_type.description: "luau" creates a Luau script (behavior, logic, converters, etc.). "wgsl" creates a shader for use with the GPU canvas. Defaults to "luau".

content.description: Optional initial source. When omitted, Luau scripts get the boilerplate for their protocol (or empty for utility) and shaders start empty. Prefer seeding here over creating empty and following up with text_editor.

scriptId.description: The id of the script/shader to rename.

scriptPath.description: Current path of the script/shader, e.g. "utils/Math3D". Use either scriptId or scriptPath.

newName.description: New leaf name only — no slashes. To relocate the file, use the move command instead.

scriptId.description: The id of the script/shader to move.

scriptPath.description: Current path of the script/shader, e.g. "utils/Math3D". Use either scriptId or scriptPath.

targetFolder.description: Destination folder path, e.g. "utils/math3d". Empty string or omitted moves to the workspace root. Folders are created if missing (mirrors create).

scriptId.description: The id of the script/shader to delete.

scriptPath.description: Path of the script/shader to delete, e.g. "utils/Math3D". Use either scriptId or scriptPath.

tools.name: text_editor
tools.description: View and edit EXISTING scripts in the workspace. STRICTLY for reading and modifying files that already exist. Do NOT use this tool to create new scripts — use create_script instead.

command.description:
The command to execute:
- view: View an existing file's contents
- str_replace: Replace text in an EXISTING file (file must already exist)
- insert: Append text to an EXISTING file (file must already exist)

path.description: The file path to operate on

old_string.description: The text to replace (for str_replace command)

view_range.description: Optional range of lines to view (1-indexed, inclusive). If provided, returns only the specified line range with line numbers prepended as "lineNumber: line".

tools.name: script_diagnostics
tools.description: Get analysis/linter errors and warnings from either a specific script if "path" is provided or all diagnostics for every script in the workspace if no path is provided

path.description: The file path to retrieve diagnostics (errors and warnings) for.

tools.name: get_scripts
tools.description: Lists all editable code files in the workspace — both Luau scripts and WGSL shaders. Each entry includes the module name, language ("luau" or "wgsl"), and (for Luau) the script protocol.

tools.name: run_tests
tools.description: Runs the tests for a given Tests script

path.description: The file path to the script to run tests for

tools.name: recompile_all_scripts
tools.description: Recompiles all scripts and updates their bytecode, committing all changes to the Luau virtual machine.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Searches for a pattern across editable code files in the workspace (Luau scripts AND WGSL shaders), similar to the grep command. Returns matching lines with their line numbers. If inclusion_set is provided, only the specified files are searched, otherwise all non-built-in files are searched. Supports case-sensitive matching, whole word matching, and regular expressions.

inclusion_set.description: Optional list of script or shader names to limit the search to. If not provided, all non-built-in files are searched.

case_sensitive.description: Whether the search should be case sensitive

match_whole_word.description: Whether to match whole words only

regular_expression.description: Whether the pattern should be treated as a regular expression

tools.name: read_console
tools.description:
Reads console output from script execution. Use this to examine print statements and errors from Rive scripts.

IMPORTANT: The console only contains output from script executions that have already occurred. If you need to see output from a specific operation:
1. Ask the user to perform the action that triggers the script (e.g., play the animation, interact with the state machine)
2. Once they confirm the action is complete, use this tool to read the results.

You can filter results by script name, entry type (print/error), or search for specific text within the output.

script_name.description: Filter entries to only those from this script

entry_type.description: Filter by entry type: 'print' for standard output, 'error' for errors

text_search.description: Case-insensitive search for text within console output

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default: 100)

offset.description: Number of matching entries to skip (for pagination)

reverse.description: When true, returns results in reverse order (newest first). Use with limit to get the most recent entries.

tools.name: get_scripting_reference
tools.description:
Retrieve Rive scripting API definitions and code examples. Use this to look up type definitions before writing code.

Request a topic key such as a builtin definition (e.g. "rive/paint", "rive/vector"), "viewmodel_definitions", "example_node", or "example_test". Use "viewmodel_definitions" when working with ViewModel data.
